chunks: 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام.
That he forbade accusing one who was outside Islam of sexual slander, unless you had directly become aware of that from him.

key_terms.اطَّلَعْتَ: you came to know directly or became aware
key_terms.ذَلِكَ: that matter, namely the accusation in question
key_terms.قَذْفِ: accusation of sexual misconduct or slander

ai.seo_question: Can a person accuse a non-Muslim of sexual misconduct without direct knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal and ethical prohibition against making accusations of sexual misconduct, even regarding someone who is not Muslim, without direct knowledge. It emphasizes restraint in speech and the protection of people's honor unless there is certain knowledge.
